clue.text: Stairs include an opening for illumination

indicators.note: the stairs word is opened up to take the next word inside it

parts.note: a flight is a run of stairs between landings

explanation.surface: A staircase is built around a window that lets in light.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanlight is the semicircular window over a door, an aperture letting daylight into a hall.

clue.text: Timor Sea — when it's rough, it produces spray

indicators.note: rough water is churned about, so the letters of the sea's name are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: The Timor Sea throws up spray when the weather turns stormy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when it's' is a link; 'rough' is the anagram signal on TIMOR SEA.
explanation.definitionFit: An atomiser is a scent or medicine bottle whose nozzle disperses liquid as a fine mist.

clue.text: Red of higher rank, one of the Great Ones

parts.note: lake is a crimson pigment, as in crimson lake
superior means senior in rank

explanation.surface: A Communist of senior standing is counted among the great figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red' looks like a Communist; it is the pigment lake. 'Great Ones' are North America's Great Lakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Superior is the largest of the five Great Lakes on the US-Canada border.

clue.text: A pale recipient of confidences

parts.note: a pale is a fence stake, and the saying 'between you and me and the ...' makes such a post the hearer of secrets

explanation.walkthrough: 'pale' looks like an adjective meaning wan; it is a noun, a wooden stake.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'between you and me and the gatepost' treats a fence upright as a confidant.

clue.text: Chap going to prison drinks in this

parts.note: Toby is a man's name, so any chap
jug is slang for jail

explanation.surface: A man heading off to jail turns to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A Toby jug is a beer mug shaped like a seated man in a tricorn hat, used for ale.

clue.text: One who knows the way put in a vehicle

indicators.note: one part is placed inside the other, here the street abbreviation goes round the vehicle

parts.note: St is short for street, a way
a van is a road vehicle

explanation.surface: A guide who knows the route is loaded into a van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the way put in a vehicle' reads as the road going inside, but here the street abbreviation wraps around the vehicle; 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A savant is a learned scholar, someone of great knowledge.

clue.text: Helps to square accounts in the field

indicators.note: parts of the two words help to make up the answer, so it lies within them

explanation.surface: Assistance with settling the books out in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'squARE Accounts'; 'in the' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A field of study or activity is an area, as in an area of expertise.

clue.text: Bird helps, they say, to provide favours

parts.note: a cock is a male bird

indicators.note: the word is spoken and spelt by its sound

parts.note: aids means helps

explanation.surface: A rooster lends a hand by handing out party gifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'favours' are rosettes worn as badges, not kindnesses.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockade is a rosette or ribbon knot worn on a hat, a kind of favour or badge.

clue.text: One who declaims "I love music"

parts.note: an orator makes speeches
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A speaker proclaims his passion for music.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratorio is a large choral work on a sacred theme, a type of composition.

clue.text: Hair fastener

definitions.meaning: a tress or curl of hair
a device securing a door with a key

explanation.definitionFit: A lock is both a tress of hair and a key-operated door bolt.

clue.text: Medieval play to elevate the maximum number of people

parts.note: Everyman is a fifteenth-century morality play
to jack up is to raise

explanation.surface: A medieval drama is staged to lift as many people as possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Every man jack' is an idiom for every single person, all without exception.

clue.text: Plant seen in Bethel

definitions.meaning: a garden perennial, the blue-flowered polemonium
in Genesis, the patriarch dreamed at Bethel of a stairway to heaven with angels

explanation.definitionFit: The name is both a flowering garden perennial and the biblical vision of a stairway that Jacob saw at Bethel.

clue.text: Used to swim in the river? That's not true

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the river's name

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river

indicators.note: swimming sets the letters moving, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone once swam in the river, or so they claim falsely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Used' looks like part of the story; it is the fodder, scrambled by 'to swim'. The Po is Italy's great river.
explanation.definitionFit: Pseudo means false or sham, pretending to be what it is not.

clue.text: A French friar, Edward, loosened the bedclothes

parts.note: un is the French for a
Friar Tuck is Robin Hood's companion
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: A French monk named Edward pulled the blankets loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Untucked describes sheets freed from being folded under the mattress.

clue.text: Barbarity demonstrated by the misuse of cutlery

indicators.note: the letters are misused, put out of their proper order

explanation.surface: Savage behaviour shown by stabbing people with knives and forks.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbarity and cruelty are synonyms for savage inhumanity.

clue.text: Regret following a star to find fulfilment

indicators.note: the regret word comes after the star word

parts.note: a comet is a shining heavenly body, loosely a star
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Sorrow after pursuing a celebrity leads to finding satisfaction.
explanation.definitionFit: A dream or wish that comes true is realised, reaching fulfilment.

clue.text: Mountaineers don't start exercises

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: climbers scale mountains

explanation.surface: Climbers who skip the warm-up routine.
explanation.definitionFit: To limber up is to stretch and warm the body before activity, so it exercises.

clue.text: August — there's risk about August 1st

indicators.note: the risk word goes round the picked letter

parts.note: to imperil is to put at risk

indicators.note: the first letter of the second August is taken

explanation.surface: A warning that August brings danger from the first of the month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there's' is a link; 'August' is the adjective meaning majestic, not the month.
explanation.definitionFit: August as an adjective means majestic and stately, like an emperor.

clue.text: The slurs spread by savage

indicators.note: the insults are spread around, so their letters are scattered

explanation.surface: Insults circulated by a brute.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruthless and savage both mean merciless and pitiless.

clue.text: 'ertfordshire town beginning to get impatient

parts.note: Hitchin is a town in Hertfordshire, England; the dropped aitch of the county tells you to drop it from the town too

indicators.note: the first letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A Cockney-sounding Hertfordshire town starts to lose patience.
explanation.walkthrough: Hitchin is a market town in Hertfordshire, a county north of London; the apostrophe marks the dropped H.
explanation.definitionFit: Itching to do something means eager and restless, impatient to start.

clue.text: Show fame isn't what it's cracked up to be

indicators.note: the letters are cracked and broken up into a new order

explanation.surface: Proof that celebrity is overrated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what it's ... to be' is link padding around the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To manifest is to display or reveal, a synonym for show as a verb.

clue.text: To outward view, everybody is about to leave union

indicators.note: the outer pair go round the leaving word
only the outside letters of the word are visible

parts.note: to quit is to leave

explanation.surface: Seemingly everyone is set to walk out of the trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To outward view' gives E and Y, the first and last letters of 'everybody', which go around QUIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Equity is the British actors' trade union.

clue.text: It's concealed by staff with good manners …

indicators.note: the small word is hidden away inside the staff word

parts.note: a pole is a staff
the word it, the possessive adding no letter

explanation.surface: Something is hidden by courteous employees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like employees; it is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Polite means courteous, having good manners.

clue.text: … both worried about ill-mannered bay horse

indicators.note: the shaken letters go round the rude word
worried letters are shaken out of order

parts.note: rough means coarse or uncouth
bay is a reddish-brown horse colour, so red

explanation.surface: A rude bay steed fretted over its stable mate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' turns BOTH into THOB, which splits around the rude word; the ellipsis links the surface to the previous clue only.
explanation.definitionFit: A thoroughbred is a pure-bred racehorse.

clue.text: Nothing works — I slipped up: there!

parts.note: zero, the letter O
ops is short for opus plural, works of music

explanation.surface: A frustrated worker admits a blunder when nothing goes right.
explanation.definitionFit: Oops is the exclamation someone makes on making a mistake.

clue.text: Passes on stamps

definitions.meaning: tools for striking coins or medals

explanation.definitionFit: Dies is both a verb for expiring and the plural of the tool used to stamp metal.

clue.text: The highest social group are out of bed by mid-morning

parts.note: up means risen
per means by, as in per post
ten o'clock is in the middle of the morning

explanation.surface: Aristocrats get up by ten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are' is a link; 'mid-morning' is a time, 10 am, not the middle letters of a word.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper ten (thousand) is an old phrase for the aristocracy, the social elite.

clue.text: 49 saw one enthuse about former king

indicators.note: the gush word goes round the king

parts.note: to gush is to enthuse
old means former
R is short for rex, king

explanation.surface: Someone in their forties gushes over a deposed monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: '49' is the year 1849, the California rush for gold, not an age.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1849 Californian stampede for gold, whose miners were called forty-niners, was one such rush.
